Messages.Author: Ashenbach
Messages.Body:
Hi all, i search the group and didn't found any answers.

Let's suppose i have a 12-copy of Ankla Hotep deck and my predator has
a Carlton Van Wyk ready. My Ankla enters combat with a vampire of my
prey, before ranges Ankla Plays Illusions of the Kindred, and in that
combat, my illusion beats the other vampire to torpor and plays
Amaranth. Then, in my predator's turn, he wants to burn Carlton to
burn my ready Ankla because he is the vampire that had commited
diablerie.

Is my ready Ankla considered the same vampire? Do i have to burn my
Ankla for Carlton's ability?

Carlton Van Wyk (Hunter)
Unique mortal with 2 life. 0 strength, 0 bleed.
Carlton can strike for 1R damage, and he may dodge as a strike once
each combat. Carlton has +1 intercept when blocking vampires. During
your discard phase, you may burn Carlton to burn a vampire who has
committed diablerie since your last turn.

Illusions of the kindred
Only usable before range is determined.
Combat ends. Move the bottom card of your crypt to your ready region.
He or she does not contest any other minions or titles in play. The
vampire has an amount of blood equal to half of his or her capacity
(round down). Combat begins between the vampire and the opposing
minion. Remove the crypt card from the game at the end of combat.
As above, but the vampire has an amount of blood equal to his or her
capacity.

Thanks in advance. :)

>
> Is my ready Ankla considered the same vampire? Do i have to burn my
> Ankla for Carlton's ability?

(...)
> Thanks in advance. :)

They are not considered the same vampire. So no, carlton cannot burn
your Ankla with your special.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Correct. (See also "turbo" decks which rely on the fact that different
copies of the same crypt card are not considered to be the same
vampire, and thus are able to bleed in a turn in which a previous copy
has bled.)
